name: Bé Chuma
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: a woman married to Conn, the king of Ireland
banished from the Otherworld for a sin
the wife of Eógan Inbir before her exile

text: Bé Chuma is a sorrowful woman from the Otherworld. Her name, from the Irish, means a woman who carries grief. She was, to tell the truth, the wife of Eógan Inbir. A sin with Gaidiar, son of Manannán mac Lir, drove her out. She lost her home and was exiled to the land of men. Conn, the king of Ireland, then took her as his own wife. Bé Chuma, however, lusted after his son Art. The druids said her acts brought a curse upon the country. She had Art sent away and treated it as a remedy. When Art came back with Delbcháem, who was his new wife, Bé Chuma had to leave Tara.

okr.objective: Describe Bé Chuma, the exiled wife of Conn who lusted after Art.
key_results: Bé Chuma was once the wife of Eógan Inbir in the Otherworld.
Her sin drove her out into the land of men.
She married Conn and then lusted after his son Art.
Bé Chuma had to depart the town of Tara when Art returned.
